newsitem.title: INDIA: India PM asks planners to aim for 7 pct GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: India PM asks planners to aim for 7 pct GDP growth.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda asked the country's plan panel on Friday to work out strategies to achieve an annual seven percent growth in gross domestic product (GDP).

"I would like the Planning Commission to work out a detailed strategy so that we can gear ourselves to achieve the seven percent growth rate," Deve Gowda said in an address to a meeting of the country's Apex planning body.
His speech was made available to Reuters.
India's GDP grew 6.6 percent in 1996/97 (April-March) as compared to 6.3 percent the previous year.
Deve Gowda, who also chairs the plan panel, said the nation should aim for a four percent growth in agriculture.
"Without a robust and fast growing agricultural sector neither economic growth nor alleviation of poverty and eradication of massive unemployment is possible," he said.
India's agriculture sector grew at 0.9 percent in 1995/96 compared to 4.9 percent in the previous year.
